sections.title: NEW ENGLAND INTO THE CAROLINAS
sections.text: SLIGHT RISK AND HIGHER WIND PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN ADJUSTED SWD THROUGH SC. OTHERWISE...CURRENT FORECAST APPEARS TO BE IN GOOD SHAPE. BROKEN BANDS OF STRONG/SEVERE TSTMS HAVE DEVELOPED THIS AFTERNOON AHEAD OF COLD FRONT PROGRESSING EWD THROUGH THE REGION. WATER VAPOR IMAGERY INDICATES THE PRESENCE OF SEVERAL SMALL-SCALE VORTICITY MAXIMA AND A 50-70 KT MIDLEVEL JET STREAK OVERSPREADING THE REGION IN ADVANCE OF PRIMARY SHORT WAVE TROUGH OVER THE UPPER GREAT LAKES INTO OH VALLEY. THIS STRENGTHENING MID/HIGH-LEVEL FLOW IS COINCIDENT WITH 40-50 KT SWLY LLJ...RESULTING IN 40-50 KT OF DEEP-LAYER SHEAR FROM THE DELMARVA INTO SRN NEW ENGLAND. THIS VERTICAL SHEAR COINCIDES WITH NRN EXTENSION OF WARM SECTOR /DELINEATED BY WARM FRONT LIFTING NWD THROUGH SRN AND CNTRL NEW ENGLAND/ WHERE A WARM AND MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER IS CONTRIBUTING TO MLCAPE OF 1000-1500 J/KG. HERE...THE POTENTIAL FOR EMBEDDED BOWING AND/OR SUPERCELL STRUCTURES WILL CONTINUE WITH THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND PERHAPS A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. FARTHER S OVER THE CAROLINAS...VERTICAL SHEAR DIMINISHES WITH SWD EXTEND...BUT COMPARABLY STRONGER INSTABILITY /MLCAPE OF 1500-2000 J PER KG/ WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORM CLUSTERS

sections.title: GREAT PLAINS
sections.text: HAIL AND TORNADO PROBABILITIES HAVE BEEN INCREASED WITHIN SLIGHT RISK AREA OVER THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. SURFACE OBSERVATIONAL DATA INDICATE THAT RICHEST BOUNDARY LAYER MOISTURE /I.E. DEWPOINTS IN THE MID TO UPPER 60S/ REMAINS CONFINED TO WRN TX...THOUGH STRENGTHENING SLY LLJ SHOULD ENHANCE THE NWD TRANSPORT OF THIS HIGHER QUALITY MOISTURE INTO PARTS OF WRN KS. THIS MOISTURE AXIS IS COLOCATED WITH ERN EXTENSION OF EML...CONTRIBUTING TO A MODERATELY UNSTABLE AIR MASS LATER THIS AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE OF 1000-2000 J/KG OVER SLIGHT RISK AREA. IT STILL APPEARS THAT TSTMS WILL BECOME FOCUSED: 1) ALONG SEWD-MOVING COLD FRONT...AND 2) E OF THE HIGHER TERRAIN OVER THE CNTRL/SRN HIGH PLAINS. THE LATTER STORM DEVELOPMENT WILL LIKELY BE ENHANCED BY MIDLEVEL IMPULSE CURRENTLY MOVING THROUGH THE CNTRL ROCKIES. WHILE STORM MODE ALONG COLD FRONT SHOULD TEND TOWARD LINEAR...THE COMBINATION OF THE MODERATE INSTABILITY AND STRENGTHENING VERTICAL SHEAR MAY SUPPORT A FEW SUPERCELLS OVER THE CNTRL/SRN HIGH PLAINS. DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND HAIL WILL BE THE MAIN SEVERE WEATHER THREATS...THOUGH A TORNADO OR TWO IS POSSIBLE WITH ANY INTENSE/LONGER-LIVED SUPERCELLS. FOR ADDITIONAL NEAR TERM GUIDANCE...SEE MCD 1

sections.title: SOUTHEAST INTO NEW ENGLAND
sections.text: YET ANOTHER IN A SERIES OF LOWER AMPLITUDE SHORTWAVE TROUGHS AND ASSOCIATED LOW/MID LEVEL JETS WILL ROTATE AROUND BROADER CENTRAL CANADA/GREAT LAKES UPPER TROUGH AND ACROSS THE NORTHEAST TODAY. LEADING IMPULSE WILL CONTINUE TO LOSE AMPLITUDE AS IT MOVES ACROSS PA EARLY TODAY...ALTHOUGH 40-50 KT MID LEVEL JET WILL MAINTAIN STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR OVER MUCH OF THE MID ATLANTIC/SRN NEW ENGLAND. SURFACE WAVE WAS EVIDENT OVER FAR NERN PA THIS MORNING WITH WARM/COASTAL FRONT EXTENDING INTO SRN NEW ENGLAND. THIS WEAK SURFACE LOW SHOULD TRACK INTO NEW ENGLAND THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AND MAINTAIN FEED OF UNSEASONABLY MOIST /NEAR TROPICAL/ AIRMASS WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR. OBSERVED AND FORECAST WIND PROFILES INDICATE FAIRLY STRONG LOW LEVEL SHEAR SPREADING FROM NERN PA/NRN NJ/FAR SRN NY ACROSS THE SRN HALF OF NEW ENGLAND UNDER 30-40 KT SSWLY H85 FLOW. ALTHOUGH AREAS OF SHOWERS/THUNDERSTORMS WILL TEND TO LIMIT HEATING AND RESULTANT DEEP INSTABILITY...LOW TOPPED SUPERCELLS REMAIN POSSIBLE WITH ATTENDANT THREATS OF ISOLATED TORNADOES AND/OR DAMAGING WINDS. FARTHER SOUTH INTO THE MID ATLANTIC AND PORTIONS OF NC...HEATING WILL BE MUCH STRONGER AND LIKELY SUPPORT AXIS OF MODERATE INSTABILITY DESPITE T

sections.title: NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: NRN STREAM SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL AMPLIFY LARGE UPPER TROUGH AS IT DIGS INTO THE NRN PLAINS TODAY...WITH RESULTANT INCREASE IN NWLY MID LEVEL FLOW DEVELOPING INTO THE CENTRAL ROCKIES/HIGH PLAINS. CONVECTION SHOULD INCREASE NEAR ASSOCIATED SURFACE COLD FRONT MOVING ACROSS THE DAKOTAS/NWRN NEB/SERN WY LATER TODAY...AS MID LEVEL CAPPING WEAKENS AND 50+F SURFACE DEW POINTS SUPPORT MARGINAL TO MODERATE INSTABILITY. ADDITIONAL...DEVELOPMENT SHOULD ALSO OCCUR ALONG AND JUST EAST OF THE CENTRAL ROCKIES INTO NRN NM WHICH WILL SPREAD OVER THE ADJACENT HIGH PLAINS THROUGH THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT. STORMS WILL LIKELY EVOLVE IN THE FORM OF CLUSTERS/LINES WITH STRONGER CORES CAPABLE OF ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS/LARGE HAIL. AT LEAST A LOW PROBABILITY THREAT WILL EXTEND NWD ALONG THE FRONT INTO ERN ND/NWRN MN...ALTHOUGH COOLER/STABLE PREFRONTAL AIR MASS SHOULD LIMIT SEVERITY WITH NRN EXTENT. NOCTURNAL ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY CONTINUE ESEWD THROUGH THE NIGHT BOTH NEAR THE SURFACE FRONT AND INVOF LOW LEVEL WAA REGIME INTO PORTIONS OF KS/OK...WITH SEVERE THREAT GRADUALLY DIMINISHING AS INSTABILITY WANES.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SERIES OF SHORTWAVES ALOFT CONTINUES TO PIVOT THROUGH BELT OF CYCLONIC FLOW AROUND MIDWESTERN/MS VALLEY LONGWAVE TROUGH. STG SHORTWAVE TROUGH -- NOW EVIDENT IN MOISTURE CHANNEL IMAGERY OVER DAKOTAS AND NERN WY -- IS FCST TO PIVOT EWD ACROSS WRN MN...NWRN IA AND ERN NEB OVERNIGHT. NRN PORTION OF TROUGH SHOULD DEVELOP CLOSED 500 MB LOW OVER NWRN ONT. RELATED AND INITIALLY WEAKER SFC LOW -- ANALYZED AT 23Z ALONG FRONT OVER NERN SD -- WILL DEEPEN CONSIDERABLY AND EJECT NEWD ACROSS NWRN AND FAR N-CENTRAL MN. TRAILING COLD FRONT -- ANALYZED AT 23Z FROM NWRN MN ACROSS E-CENTRAL/SERN SD...W-CENTRAL NEB AND SERN WY -- IS FCST TO MOVE INTO WRN WI...ERN THROUGH SWRN IA...NERN MO...CENTRAL KS...AND SERN CO/NERN NM BY END OF PERIOD. ERN CONUS COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE EWD OVERNIGHT ACROSS NEW ENGLAND...OFFSHORE MID-ATLANTIC REGION. SRN PORTION OF FRONT WILL DECELERATE AND WEAKEN ACROSS PIEDMONT REGION OF CAROLINAS/GA...AND WILL REMAIN QUASISTATIONARY WWD OVER CENTRAL/SRN PORTIONS AL/MS. WRN-MOST SEGMENT OF FRONT HAS BECOME DIFFUSE OVER CENTRAL TX...AND WILL RETREAT NWD THROUGH REMAINDER PERIOD.

sections.title: MN TO SRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: BAND OF STG-SVR TSTMS HAS DEVELOPED ALONG/AHEAD OF SFC COLD FRONT FROM NWRN MN SWWD ACROSS NEB. REF WW 647 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS FOR NEAR-TERM DETAILS. SVR POTENTIAL INCREASES AND WILL LAST LONGER INTO EVENING FROM N-S ACROSS THIS CORRIDOR...IN PROXIMITY TO RICHER LOW LEVEL MOISTURE AND RESULTING GREATER BUOYANCY...WITHIN ENVIRONMENT OF AT LEAST MRGLLY FAVORABLE DEEP-LAYER SHEAR. TSTMS ALSO WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP AND MOVE EWD IN SWATH FROM NWRN KS AND SWRN NEB SWWD ACROSS ERN NM IN TWO PRIMARY REGIMES... 1. OROGRAPHICALLY INITIATED CONVECTION...SOME OF WHICH ALREADY HAS ACCUMULATED ORGANIZED COLD POOLS OVER ERN CO AND NERN NM...AND 2. WIDELY SCATTERED TSTMS FARTHER E ACROSS SWRN NEB AND WRN KS...IN CLOSER PROXIMITY TO WELL-DEFINED LOW LEVEL MOISTURE/THETAE AXIS THAT IS ANALYZED FROM ROUGHLY LTS-GCK-EAR-FSD. THESE INCLUDE A FEW SUPERCELLS WITH DAMAGING GUST/HAIL POTENTIAL UNTIL MODE BECOMES MORE LINEAR OR CLUSTERED. TORNADO RISK IS CONDITIONAL ON STORM MODE AND STORM-SCALE PROCESSES...AND IS MAINLY DURING NEXT 2-3 HOURS AS MOISTURE ADVECTION OFFSETS SFC DIABATIC COOLING ENOUGH TO KEEP INFLOW-LAYER PARCELS NEARLY SFC BASED. OFFSETTING FACTOR S OF ABOUT KS/NEB BORDER WIL

sections.title: MID-ATLANTIC TO TIDEWATER AND OUTER BANKS
sections.text: SVR POTENTIAL IS DECREASING ACROSS THIS AREA AS AIR MASS STABILIZES FROM COMBINED EFFECTS OF DIABATIC SFC COOLING AND -- IN SOME AREAS -- ANTECEDENT CONVECTIVE PROCESSES. REMAINING POTENTIAL SHOULD BE IN FORM OF ISOLATED DAMAGING GUSTS. ..EDWARDS.. 08/01/2009
